title: Dispelling the myth of violence and mental illness (SOP27)

sentences.en: The state of a perpetrator's mental health is often the focus of news reports in the aftermath of mass shootings and other acts of violence.
sentences.zh: 在大规模枪击事件和其他暴力行为发生后，凶手的心理健康状况往往是新闻报道的焦点。

sentences.en: Legislators and the public want to be able to predict if and when a person will become violent.
sentences.zh: 立法者和公众希望能够预测一个人是否会以及何时会变得暴力。

sentences.en: In this episode, forensic psychologist Joel DeVoskin talks about why the stigma surrounding mental health is to blame
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，法医心理学家乔尔·德沃斯金（Joel DeVoskin）将探讨为什么围绕心理健康的污名化是罪魁祸首，

sentences.en: and also how psychologists can help prevent more violence if they are just given the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 以及如果给予机会，心理学家将如何帮助防止更多的暴力事件。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿（Audrey Hamilton），这里是《心理学话语》（Speaking of Psychology）。

sentences.en: Joel DeVoskin teaches in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Arizona.
sentences.zh: 乔尔·德沃斯金在亚利桑那大学精神病学系任教。

sentences.en: He is chairman of the Governor's Advisory Council on Behavioral Health for the state of Nevada.
sentences.zh: 他是内华达州州长行为健康咨询委员会的主席。

sentences.en: He's also a clinical and forensic psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是一名临床和法医心理学家。

sentences.en: He's served as an expert witness in several state and federal courts throughout the U.S., and he specializes in assessing a person's risk of violence to self and others,
sentences.zh: 他曾在美国多个州和联邦法院担任专家证人，专注于评估一个人对自我及他人实施暴力的风险，

sentences.en: as well as workplace violence prevention.
sentences.zh: 以及工作场所暴力预防。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. DeVoskin.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，德沃斯金博士。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加节目。

sentences.en: There have been several high-profile shootings in the news where the suspect has been described as having some sort of mental disorder, either officially or anecdotally.
sentences.zh: 新闻中曾报道过几起备受瞩目的枪击事件，其中嫌疑人被官方或传言描述为患有某种精神障碍。

sentences.en: What sort of message is this sending to the general public about the association between mental illness and violence?
sentences.zh: 这向广大公众传达了关于精神疾病与暴力之间联系的什么信息？

sentences.en: Is there a link?
sentences.zh: 它们之间真的有联系吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of messages that it sends, and some of them are very inaccurate and, in fact, counterproductive and harmful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它传达了许多信息，其中一些非常不准确，甚至适得其反且有害。

sentences.en: The short version is that while people with serious mental illness are slightly more likely to commit acts of violence than people without mental illness,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，虽然患有严重精神疾病的人实施暴力行为的可能性比没有精神疾病的人略高，

sentences.en: the risk that it creates is pretty small compared to other known risk factors, for example, current substance abuse.
sentences.zh: 但与其他已知的风险因素（例如当前滥用药物）相比，它所产生的风险其实非常小。

sentences.en: It's also true that a lot of the people that you read about, these anecdotes are played up by the media, and people overgeneralize from these very dramatic examples.
sentences.zh: 同样真实的是，你在新闻中读到的许多人，这些轶事都被媒体夸大了，人们会从这些极具戏剧性的例子中过度概括。

sentences.en: So when you see somebody do something horrible, you think it happens more often than it actually does.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你看到某人做出可怕的事情时，你会认为这种事发生的频率比实际情况更高。

sentences.en: So the facts are pretty clear that, first of all, mass homicide accounts for a very tiny percentage of all the gun deaths in the United States, like 1 or 2 percent.
sentences.zh: 所以事实非常清楚，首先，大规模凶杀案仅占美国所有枪支死亡人数极小的一部分，大约占1%或2%。

sentences.en: And even homicide is less of a problem in terms of gun deaths than suicide.
sentences.zh: 而且，就枪支死亡人数而言，凶杀案带来的问题其实比自杀还要少。

sentences.en: Another example is where the electronic media focus on long guns, like Bushmasters and assault weapons.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是，电子媒体专注于长枪，例如大毒蛇（Bushmaster）突击武器。

sentences.en: They account for a very small percentage of gun violence in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它们只占美国枪支暴力极小的一部分。

sentences.en: The vast majority of gun violence has to do with handguns.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数枪支暴力都与手枪有关。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of misinformation, and the press only cares about selling, or not the press, but the electronic media, mainly cable news, mainly care about selling airtime.
sentences.zh: 因此存在大量错误信息，媒体关心的只是销售，或者说不是媒体，而是电子媒体，主要是有限电视新闻，主要关心的是出售播出时间。

sentences.en: So they put on the things that are the most dramatic, and that causes people to overgeneralize.
sentences.zh: 因此他们会播放最具戏剧性的内容，这会导致人们过度概括。

sentences.en: The results of that is that it creates additional stigma about mental illness and actually discourages people from getting treatment.
sentences.zh: 其结果是，它对精神疾病产生了额外的污名化，实际上阻碍了人们去寻求治疗。

sentences.en: So it's bad for a lot of reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以由于很多原因，这都是不好的。

sentences.en: What role does mental health stigma play in the debate over gun violence and gun policy, specifically stigma?
sentences.zh: 心理健康污名化在关于枪支暴力和枪支政策的辩论中扮演了什么角色，特别是指污名化？

sentences.en: Well, again, the politicians have an unfortunate tendency to react to what is most publicized and also to react to anecdotes as opposed to solid research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，同样的，政客们有一种不幸的倾向，即对最受宣传的事情做出反应，并且对轶事做出反应，而不是基于坚实的研究。

sentences.en: And we don't know enough to really guide public policy.
sentences.zh: 而且我们了解得还不够多，无法真正指导公共政策。

sentences.en: So stigma, which is sort of a collection of myths and stereotypes,
sentences.zh: 因此，某种程度上由神话和刻板印象组成的污名化，

sentences.en: tends to guide public policy far too much.
sentences.zh: 往往过多地指导了公共政策。

sentences.en: And as I said, much of it's incorrect.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，其中大部分是不正确的。

sentences.en: So we end up with policies that people tout as saying we did something, but in fact it's either not helpful or in some cases counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们最终得到的政策是人们吹嘘说我们做了一些事情，但事实上这些政策要么没有帮助，要么在某些情况下适得其反。

sentences.en: And we'd be far better off as a country if, instead of relying on stigma, people were encouraging really good research about how to reduce gun violence
sentences.zh: 如果人们不是依靠污名化，而是鼓励真正好的研究来了解如何减少枪支暴力，那对我们国家会好得多，

sentences.en: rather than just react to these extreme cases and the stigma and myths and stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅对这些极端案例以及污名化、神话和刻板印象做出反应。

sentences.en: An example of this, you know, some legislators have been pressing for laws that prevent the sale of firearms to anyone who has ever been diagnosed with a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这方面的一个例子，你知道的，一些立法者一直在敦促制定法律，禁止向任何曾被诊断患有精神疾病的人出售枪支。

sentences.en: Should mental health be taken into account when deciding who can own a firearm?
sentences.zh: 在决定谁可以拥有枪支时，是否应将心理健康考虑在内？

sentences.en: If a person has schizophrenia, the likelihood that they will kill a stranger has been estimated, according to research, at 1 in 144,000.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人患有精神分裂症，根据研究估计，他杀死陌生人的可能性是14.4万分之一。

sentences.en: So it's popular for politicians to say, oh, I did something.
sentences.zh: 因此，政客们喜欢说，哦，我做了一些事情。

sentences.en: You know, the myth is you'd have to be, quote, crazy to do something like this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种神话是，你必须是“疯狂的”才会做出这样的事情。

sentences.en: So retrospectively, you look at people and you say, wow, this obviously, that guy should have been branded.
sentences.zh: 所以事后回顾起来，你看着这些人，然后说，哇，显然这个人早就该被贴上标签了。

sentences.en: But the truth is that most of the people, even of these anecdotes, were people who were very early on in their illness who had not been identified as seriously mentally ill,
sentences.zh: 但事实是，大多数人，甚至是这些被广为流传的人，都是那些病情处于早期、尚未被认定为患有严重精神疾病的人，

sentences.en: who wouldn't have been on the list anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何他们都不会在名单上。

sentences.en: There's a couple of exceptions to that.
sentences.zh: 对此有几个例外情况。

sentences.en: So for the most part, it's just stuff that's easy to sell as to say, I did something really important.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大多数情况下，这些只是很容易兜售的东西，好让人说，我做了一件非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: But alcohol accounts for a great deal more violence than mental illness does.
sentences.zh: 但酒精引发的暴力事件远比精神疾病要多得多。

sentences.en: As a forensic psychologist who assesses people who might be a risk to themselves or to others, what challenges do you face in determining who will become dangerous?
sentences.zh: 作为一名评估可能对自己或他人构成风险的法医心理学家，在确定谁会变得危险时，你面临着哪些挑战？

sentences.en: Well, there's a whole bunch of research about assessing the risk of dangerousness that looks at the traits of a person.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多关于评估危险行为风险的研究，这些研究着眼于人的特征。

sentences.en: But we know that all human behavior is an interaction between a human being and the circumstances or situations in which they find themselves.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，所有人类行为都是人与他们所处的环境或处境之间相互作用的结果。

sentences.en: And it's very difficult to predict the situations that a person's going to be in in the future.
sentences.zh: 而且很难预测一个人未来将处于什么处境。

sentences.en: We think that a better strategy is when you become aware of a person who is either uttering or posing threats
sentences.zh: 我们认为，更好的策略是，当你发现有人在发表或构成威胁时，

sentences.en: is then to look at the person in the context of the situation they're in and make recommendations to intervene and change that situation.
sentences.zh: 就要将这个人置于他们所处的环境背景中去审视，并提出干预和改变这种环境的建议。

sentences.en: Steve Hart, one of my colleagues and friends, calls these risk scenarios, is under what circumstances would this person be likely to harm somebody?
sentences.zh: 我的同事兼朋友史蒂夫·哈特（Steve Hart）称这些为风险情境，即在什么情况下这个人更有可能伤害他人？

sentences.en: That's much more helpful than saying this guy's a high-risk person based on these sort of all-or-nothing determinations.
sentences.zh: 这比根据这种非此即彼的判定说这家伙是个高风险人员要有帮助得多。

sentences.en: But there are a number of different methods of risk assessment, and many of them are really good.
sentences.zh: 但风险评估的方法有很多种，其中许多确实很好。

sentences.en: Some are actuarial, which help you look at the kind of overall risk that a person might present.
sentences.zh: 有些是精算式的，这有助于你了解一个人可能呈现的整体风险。

sentences.en: But it won't tell you under what circumstances they will or won't.
sentences.zh: 但它不会告诉你他们在什么情况下会或不会这样做。

sentences.en: So even if you knew that somebody had a 50% chance, was in a group of people with a 50% chance of being violent, you don't know if they're in the 50 that will or the 50 that won't,
sentences.zh: 因此，即使你知道某人有50%的几率，处于具有50%暴力倾向的人群中，你也不知道他们是那50%会实施暴力的人，还是那50%不会实施暴力的人，

sentences.en: and it may depend on the situations in which they find themselves.
sentences.zh: 这可能取决于他们发现自己所处的情境。

sentences.en: When you do risk assessment, risk assessment by itself isn't very important.
sentences.zh: 当你做风险评估时，风险评估本身并不是最重要的。

sentences.en: What matters is the steps that are taken as a result.
sentences.zh: 重要的是作为结果所采取的步骤。

sentences.en: So that could be treatment, it could be intervening in the situations, it could be skill teaching for people.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是治疗，可能是干预情境，也可能是对人们进行技能培训。

sentences.en: Their goal is no longer to call people names, it's to actually prevent violence.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标不再是给人们贴标签，而是真正地预防暴力。

sentences.en: What ways can mental health services be more effective in assessing and treating people who could present a danger to themselves or others?
sentences.zh: 心理健康服务可以通过哪些方式在评估和治疗可能对自身或他人构成危险的人方面发挥更大作用？

sentences.en: Well, in my opinion, the most important role of the public mental health system in preventing violence is not related to the treatment of serious mental illness,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，公共心理健康系统在预防暴力方面最重要的作用与严重精神疾病的治疗无关，

sentences.en: although that's very important for clinical reasons.
sentences.zh: 尽管出于临床原因这非常重要。

sentences.en: But where we really want to see the public mental health system better funded and better capable of intervening is in crisis response.
sentences.zh: 但我们真正希望看到公共心理健康系统获得更多资金并具备更强干预能力的地方是在危机应对上。

sentences.en: So when somebody feels depressed, enraged, insignificant, they have access to a firearm,
sentences.zh: 因此，当某人感到抑郁、愤怒、无足轻重，他们可以接触到枪支，

sentences.en: maybe they're drinking too much that night, maybe they just got fired, and so it's like this perfect storm of despair.
sentences.zh: 也许他们那天晚上喝了太多酒，也许他们刚刚被解雇，所以这就好比是一场绝望的完美风暴。

sentences.en: It would be very important for our system to be able to give that person really competent suicide prevention services in this crisis
sentences.zh: 对于我们的系统来说，能够在这次危机中为这个人提供真正称职的预防自杀服务，将是非常重要的，

sentences.en: to give them an alternative to ending their life as a way of ending their psychological pain.
sentences.zh: 为他们提供一种替代终结生命的方式，作为摆脱心理痛苦的途径。

sentences.en: And that's something, and it's not a criticism of the people who are doing this work, there's some wonderful first responders, both in mental health and paramedics and police.
sentences.zh: 这是一件事，这并非对从事这项工作的人的批评，有一些非常出色的急救人员，包括心理健康领域的、医护人员和警察。

sentences.en: But if you get good at this, you can't keep doing it because the pay is not very good.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在这方面变得优秀，你就无法坚持下去，因为薪水并不高。

sentences.en: If you want to raise a family, people quit those jobs and go on to other things so they can make better living.
sentences.zh: 如果你想养家糊口，人们就会辞掉这些工作去干别的，这样他们才能维持更好的生计。

sentences.en: So we need more money so we can have more timely, more competent crisis response services by the public mental health as well as other first responder systeMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要更多的资金，以便公共心理健康系统以及其他急救系统能够提供更及时、更有能力的危机应对服务。

sentences.en: And that would, I think, every time somebody commits a mass homicide, they're ending their life.
sentences.zh: 我认为，每次有人实施大规模凶杀时，他们都在结束自己的生命。

sentences.en: They're either going to commit suicide or they're going to get the police to shoot them or they're going to go to prison or hospital for the rest of their life.
sentences.zh: 他们要么自杀，要么让警察枪杀他们，要么余生都在监狱或医院度过。

sentences.en: They've given up.
sentences.zh: 他们已经放弃了。

sentences.en: Their life is over.
sentences.zh: 他们的人生已经结束了。

sentences.en: And we know how to prevent suicide.
sentences.zh: 我们知道如何预防自杀。

sentences.en: We just don't do it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是没有去做。

sentences.en: We know a ton about suicide prevention, and yet the suicide rates in the United States haven't gone down because we haven't made a good societal investment in suicide prevention
sentences.zh: 我们对自杀预防了解得非常多，然而美国的自杀率并没有下降，因为我们没有对自杀预防和危机应对进行良好的社会投资。

sentences.en: and crisis responding.
sentences.zh: 危机应对。

sentences.en: And that, I feel, is very important and would make a very big difference.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常重要，会产生非常大的影响。

sentences.en: I also would say that we need a lot more information and data, and Congress has, to an unfortunate extent, stifled research on preventing gun violence.
sentences.zh: 我还想说，我们需要更多的信息和数据，而国会在很大程度上扼杀了关于预防枪支暴力的研究。

sentences.en: So the National Violent Death Reporting System only exists in, I think, 16 states.
sentences.zh: 因此，国家暴力死亡报告系统（National Violent Death Reporting System）据我所知只存在于16个州。

sentences.en: That should be nationwide.
sentences.zh: 这应该在全国范围内推广。

sentences.en: CDC, the Center for Disease Control, is discouraged from doing research on gun violence.
sentences.zh: 疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）被劝阻不要进行枪支暴力方面的研究。

sentences.en: And it's not about the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这与宪法第二修正案无关。

sentences.en: There's going to be guns in the streets of America for as long as I'm alive.
sentences.zh: 只要我还活着，美国的街道上就会一直有枪支。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that we can't learn more about how to prevent violent use of these guns and inappropriate use of these guns through a variety of mechanisms,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我们不能通过各种机制来更多地了解如何防止这些枪支的暴力使用和不当使用，

sentences.en: including public information, training, safety training.
sentences.zh: 包括公共信息、培训、安全培训。

sentences.en: There's a lot of different things that we...
sentences.zh: 有很多不同的事情我们……

sentences.en: And we just don't know which things work because there hasn't been enough research done.
sentences.zh: 而我们只是不知道哪些事情管用，因为没有进行足够的研究。

sentences.en: Okay, Dr. DeVoskin, thank you so much for taking the time to speak with us.
sentences.zh: 好的，德沃斯金博士，非常感谢您抽出时间与我们交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate your having me.
sentences.zh: 我很感激您邀请我来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您。

sentences.en: For more information on DeVoskin's research and to hear more episodes, go to our website, speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 有关德沃斯金研究的更多信息并收听更多节目，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: With the American Psychological Association's
sentences.zh: 这里是美国心理学协会的

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology, I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话语》，我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。
